title: Account deletion policy tabletop
policy_source: ADR 0013, owner decisions recorded in docs/dev/behavior-parity-review.md, and current account-deletion implementation.
schema_basis: Current ORM/Alembic schema and disposable PostgreSQL tests; no deployed operator database was inspected.

scenarios.classification: source-reviewed; role-specific runtime case not separately exercised
scenarios.outcome: The shared deletion service removes account-linked private rows and credentials, retains shared rows under their declared disposition, and queues owned files after the database transaction. The deletion service has no child-specific data-retention branch. The R1989 fixture exercises the common service using a regular user and a surviving admin.
scenarios.limits: A dedicated child-role account-deletion test was not run. Existing child save-access policy is independent of this deletion disposition.

scenarios.classification: confirmed by focused PostgreSQL concurrency regression
scenarios.outcome: Two concurrent native admin deletions serialize; one succeeds and the other is denied after the actor is no longer active, leaving one active admin.
scenarios.limits: This protects the final active admin in the tested route and transaction path; deployed-schema qualification remains open.

scenarios.scenario: shared channel or space owner departs
scenarios.outcome: Shared chat spaces and channels are retained with creator references cleared; the departing member's membership rows are deleted. Shared messages remain and render with the anonymous member label, while that member's attachment metadata and uploaded bytes are deleted after commit.
scenarios.limits: The tests use synthetic current-schema rows and do not inspect a deployed household database.

scenarios.outcome: DownloadRequest rows are deleted. Their file_location and zip_file_path refer to game/library source content selected by download routes and constrained to configured library roots; they are not user-owned download copies. Account deletion must preserve those shared library files.
scenarios.limits: No separate test asserts the source file bytes through a download request; the deletion file-candidate inventory excludes DownloadRequest paths and protects the explicitly managed user-file classes.

scenarios.scenario: external store disconnect during account deletion
scenarios.classification: local unlink confirmed; provider-side revocation unknown
scenarios.outcome: The departing account's StoreAccount rows, encrypted credential material, and owned-title rows are deleted locally by declared account cascades. The surviving account's linked-store rows are preserved. The shared deletion service makes no provider HTTP revocation call.
scenarios.limits: Local credential deletion prevents Oneirodex from using the credential, but does not establish that the third party invalidates it. Provider revocation behavior and whether account deletion should attempt provider-specific revocation remain unverified.

verification.source_review: Completed for all five scenarios listed above.
verification.focused_tests: Existing R1987-R1990 PostgreSQL regression results support the referenced outcomes; no code changed for this tabletop.
verification.bundle_validator: The R1972 seven-report validator was rerun and passed; R1991 is a separate follow-up artifact outside that immutable bundle.
remaining: Decide and implement provider-specific remote token revocation if required; do not infer remote revocation from local credential deletion.
Compare deployed operator schema and exercise restore/reapplication and production restart only under separately authorized operations.
